big_ideas.title: Probabilities are free energies
big_ideas.text: Every observable is a Boltzmann-weighted average, and every free-energy difference is a log of a population or partition-function ratio. Turning counts into kcal/mol and back is the core move of the field.

big_ideas.title: The answer is only as good as the model
big_ideas.text: A force field, water model, protonation state, box and cutoff scheme define the Hamiltonian being sampled. They are one package; change one piece and the results belong to a different model.

big_ideas.title: Dynamics is a sampling engine
big_ideas.text: Integrators, constraints, thermostats and barostats exist to generate the right ensemble stably and efficiently. Their parameters trade accuracy, speed and fidelity of the dynamics.

big_ideas.title: Finite, correlated sampling sets the error bar
big_ideas.text: Trajectories are correlated time series of finite length. The number of independent samples, not the number of frames, sets the uncertainty, and unvisited states produce error no error bar shows.

big_ideas.title: Free energy is a state function
big_ideas.text: Because ΔG depends only on endpoints, non-physical alchemical paths and thermodynamic cycles give physical answers. Good paths keep neighbouring states overlapping.

big_ideas.title: Alchemical space can be sampled like real space
big_ideas.text: λ dynamics treats λ as a coordinate with its own dynamics; with implicit constraints and flattened biases, one simulation visits many chemical end states, and their populations give the free energies.

big_ideas.title: Simulation is a reproducible pipeline
big_ideas.text: Results come from scripts run on shared clusters. Correct scheduling, engine choice, bookkeeping and documentation decide whether a number can be trusted, repeated and published.

practices.title: Define the system and ensemble
practices.text: State what physical question is asked, which ensemble and endpoints answer it, and which states (folded/unfolded, bound/unbound) must be simulated.

practices.title: Build the model
practices.text: Choose force field, water, protonation and tautomer states, termini, ions, box shape and size, and write them down.

practices.title: Choose the method and its parameters
practices.text: Pick integrator, timestep, constraints, thermostat, barostat, electrostatics, estimator, λ schedule or ALF options to fit the goal, and check each against its validity conditions.

practices.title: Compute with units
practices.text: kcal/mol and k_BT, Å and nm, fs/ps/ns, steps vs time, molar vs per-molecule; never mix them silently.

practices.title: Check and quantify
practices.text: Sanity-check limits and magnitudes, test equilibration and convergence, estimate uncertainty from independent samples, and close cycles.

practices.title: Run, script and document
practices.text: Write and debug engine scripts and job files, run them on the cluster, and keep every input needed to reproduce the result.

los.do: Choose the ensemble (NVE, NVT, NPT, μVT) that matches a described experiment or simulation goal — choice rep.
ek: Bench conditions (fixed T and P) ⇒ NPT, whose free energy is G; NVT gives A; NVE conserves H and is used to test integrators and measure unperturbed dynamics.

los.do: State the ergodic hypothesis and identify features of a system that break it on simulation timescales.
ek: Time average = ensemble average only if the trajectory visits all relevant states; barriers of many k_BT (slow rotamers, buried waters, unfolding) make runs quasi-nonergodic.

los.do: Calculate the instantaneous temperature from kinetic energy and the count of degrees of freedom — numeric rep.
ek: ⟨K⟩ = (N_df/2) k_B T; N_df = 3N − N_constraints − 3 when centre-of-mass motion is removed.

los.do: Calculate the population ratio of two states from their energy difference at a given temperature — numeric rep.
ek: p_i/p_j = exp[−(E_i − E_j)/k_BT]; k_BT = 0.593 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, so 1.36 kcal/mol is a factor of 10.

los.do: Convert between a population (or probability) ratio and a free-energy difference — numeric rep.
ek: ΔG_A→B = −k_BT ln(P_B/P_A); a free energy counts every microstate of a state, so it includes entropy, not just the lowest energy.

los.do: Distinguish Helmholtz and Gibbs free energy and the potential of mean force along a coordinate, and state which one a given simulation yields.
ek: A = −k_BT ln Q (NVT), G = −k_BT ln Δ (NPT); W(ξ) = −k_BT ln P(ξ) + const. Absolute Q is intractable, but ratios of Q are ensemble averages.

los.do: Write the CHARMM potential energy function term by term and name each parameter and the pairs each term excludes.
ek: Bonds K_b(b − b₀)², angles K_θ(θ − θ₀)², Urey–Bradley, dihedrals K_φ[1 + cos(nφ − δ)], impropers, CMAP, LJ ε[(R_min/r)¹² − 2(R_min/r)⁶], Coulomb; 1-2 and 1-3 pairs excluded, 1-4 pairs use special LJ parameters.

los.do: Calculate a Lennard-Jones or Coulomb pair energy from CHARMM parameters using the combining rules — numeric rep.
ek: ε_ij = √(ε_i ε_j), R_min,ij = R_min,i/2 + R_min,j/2; Coulomb = 332.06 q_i q_j / r kcal/mol with r in Å and q in e.

los.do: Explain what RTF, PRM, PSF, CRD and toppar.str files each contain and which ones CHARMM reads in what order.
ek: RTF: atoms, types, charges, connectivity and patches per residue (which terms exist); PRM: the constants in those terms; PSF: the generated list of atoms, bonds, angles, dihedrals of this system; CRD: coordinates; toppar.str streams the RTF/PRM set.

los.do: Map a residue's chemical state to its CHARMM36 name or patch: ASPP, GLUP, HSD/HSE/HSP, LSN, NTER/CTER, ACE/CT3 — choice rep.
ek: ASP, GLU deprotonated and LYS protonated by default; HIS must always be specified; charged termini for a whole protein, neutral ACE/CT3 caps for a peptide cut from a chain.

los.do: Describe how CHARMM36/CGenFF charges, dihedrals and LJ parameters are fitted, and why water model, cutoffs, constraints and 1-4 treatment belong to the parameter set.
ek: Charges fit to QM interaction energies with TIP3P water; dihedrals to QM scans; LJ to liquid densities and heats of vaporization. Constraint and cutoff settings are part of the force field definition — match the parameterizing work.

los.do: Judge a CGenFF (ParamChem) parameter assignment from its penalty scores and decide whether to validate or reoptimize — choice rep.
ek: Penalty < 10 ≈ fine; 10–50 validate; > 50 reparameterize against QM.

los.do: Compare TIP3P (CHARMM variant), SPC/E and TIP4P-type models by geometry, rigidity and known property errors, and name the model CHARMM36 assumes.
ek: TIP3P: rigid 3-site; the CHARMM variant adds LJ on H; diffuses ~2× too fast but CHARMM36 is fitted with it. TIP4P models add a virtual M site carrying the negative charge.

los.do: Write one step of velocity Verlet and of leapfrog and explain why their time reversibility and symplecticity give bounded energy error.
ek: Leapfrog: v(t + ½Δt) = v(t − ½Δt) + a(t)Δt, x(t + Δt) = x(t) + v(t + ½Δt)Δt. Symplectic integrators conserve a shadow Hamiltonian, so NVE energy fluctuates without drift; drift signals a bad Δt or cutoff artifacts.

los.do: Advance positions and velocities through one or two integration steps for a given 1-D force — numeric rep.
ek: Velocity Verlet: x₁ = x₀ + v₀Δt + ½a₀Δt²; v₁ = v₀ + ½(a₀ + a₁)Δt.

los.do: Calculate the period of the fastest vibration from its wavenumber and pick the largest stable timestep with and without hydrogen-bond constraints — numeric rep.
ek: T = 1/(c ν̃); X–H stretches at 3000–3600 cm⁻¹ have T ≈ 9–11 fs; with Δt ≲ T/10 that is ~1 fs unconstrained, ~2 fs with X–H constrained (rigid water roughly doubles Δt).

los.do: Explain how SHAKE, RATTLE and SETTLE impose holonomic constraints and count the degrees of freedom they remove.
ek: Lagrange multipliers iteratively restore bond lengths each step; SETTLE solves rigid 3-site water analytically; each constraint removes one degree of freedom (enters N_df).

los.do: Decide when to use hydrogen mass repartitioning at 4 fs, or drop constraints and use 1 fs, including for bonds to alchemical atoms — choice rep.
ek: HMR moves mass from heavy atoms to their H, conserving total mass and thermodynamics but altering kinetics. Constraints on bonds that change length between alchemical states bias single-topology results; 1 fs without them is the general fix.

los.do: Diagnose an unstable timestep or bad starting structure from run symptoms (SHAKE failures, energy blow-up, temperature spikes).
ek: Early crashes usually mean unrelaxed contacts (minimize) or too large a Δt; steady NVE drift means Δt, constraint tolerance or cutoff treatment is too loose.

los.do: Choose a thermostat for a stated goal — fast equilibration, canonical production, or dynamical properties — and justify it — choice rep.
ek: Bussi: general purpose; Nosé–Hoover chains: canonical, better ergodicity in small systems; Langevin: canonical, robust, damps dynamics; Berendsen and simple velocity rescaling give the wrong ensemble (flying ice cube).

los.do: Write the Langevin equation and explain how the friction coefficient (CHARMM fbeta, ps⁻¹) trades temperature control against dynamical fidelity.
ek: m dv/dt = F − γmv + R(t), ⟨R(t)R(t′)⟩ = 2γm k_BT δ(t − t′). BLaDE uses a g-BAOAB Langevin integrator; the tutorial's fbeta 0.1 ps⁻¹ is weak coupling.

los.do: Choose a barostat for equilibration vs production and for isotropic vs anisotropic cells — choice rep.
ek: Berendsen only for early equilibration; Monte Carlo barostat, Langevin piston and Parrinello–Rahman sample NPT; anisotropic or semi-isotropic coupling for membranes and crystals.

los.do: Explain how a Monte Carlo barostat accepts a volume move and set its BLaDE parameters (prmc, iprs, pref, prdv).
ek: Accept with min{1, exp[−β(ΔU + PΔV) + N ln(V′/V)]}; BLaDE's N counts heavy atoms. iprs = steps between attempts (default 50), pref = pressure in atm (1), prdv = σ of ΔV in Å³ (100).

los.do: Calculate a system's density from its box dimensions and total mass and check it against the expected value — numeric rep.
ek: ρ = M/(N_A V); 1 g/cm³ = 0.6022 amu/Å³. Pure TIP3P at 298 K should sit near 0.98–1.0 g/cm³.

topics.title: Periodic boundary conditions and box choice

los.do: Apply the minimum-image convention to find the distance between two atoms in a periodic box — numeric rep.
ek: Δx ← Δx − L·round(Δx/L) per axis; valid only when the nonbonded cutoff is below L/2.

los.do: Size a solvent box from the solute's extent and edge distance and compare atom counts for cubic, truncated-octahedral and rhombic-dodecahedral cells — numeric rep.
ek: Cube side = d_max + 2 × edge (10 Å is standard; more for highly charged solutes like RNA). For the same image distance d: V_cube = d³, V_oct ≈ 0.770 d³ (23% fewer atoms), V_RD ≈ 0.707 d³ (29% fewer). Water ≈ 0.0334 molecules/Å³.

los.do: Explain why periodic artifacts are smaller than vacuum-interface artifacts and name the cases where they are not.
ek: A droplet's surface distorts the solute; images avoid it. Artifacts grow with net charge, small boxes, and solutes that expand (unfolded chains need a fixed, larger box, e.g. 40 Å for the pentapeptides).

los.do: Explain why truncating Coulomb interactions fails in condensed phases and how Ewald splitting into real- and reciprocal-space sums fixes it.
ek: 1/r decays slower than the number of neighbours grows (∝ r²). Ewald: erfc(κr)/r is short-ranged in real space; the smooth remainder is summed on a reciprocal grid (PME, O(N log N)); a uniform neutralizing background handles net charge.

los.do: Choose PME parameters (real-space cutoff, κ, grid spacing, interpolation order) consistent with a target accuracy — choice rep.
ek: Typical CHARMM36 setup: 12 Å cutoff, κ ≈ 0.34 Å⁻¹, grid spacing ≤ 1 Å, order 4–6 (BLaDE supports 4, 6, 8). Larger κ shifts work to reciprocal space.

los.do: Distinguish switched, shifted and force-switched LJ cutoffs and pick the CHARMM36 standard, including neighbour-list buffer.
ek: CHARMM36: vfswitch from 10 to 12 Å, pair list to 14–16 Å; BLaDE requires PME or VSWITCH for electrostatics and VFSWITCH or VSHIFT for LJ. Apply long-range dispersion corrections only if the force field was fitted with them.

los.do: Assign protonation states from propka pKa predictions at the experimental pH, using predicted pKa for the folded state and model pKa for an unfolded peptide — numeric rep.
ek: pH < pKa ⇒ protonated; fraction protonated = 1/(1 + 10^(pH − pKa)). Check ASP, GLU, HIS, LYS; ARG, TYR, CYS rarely titrate. Record the states — they go in the methods section.

los.do: Choose a histidine tautomer (HSD, HSE, HSP) from its pKa and hydrogen-bond environment — choice rep.
ek: Protonated ⇒ HSP; otherwise put H on the δ or ε N according to nearby donors/acceptors; HSE when exposed or unclear (marginally more stable in the unfolded state).

los.do: Calculate the number of counterions and salt ion pairs needed to neutralize a box and reach a target concentration — numeric rep.
ek: N_pairs ≈ c(M) × V(Å³) × 6.022 × 10⁻⁴; neutralize the net solute charge first. Mimic the experiment; otherwise ~150 mM (Na⁺ extracellular, K⁺ intracellular).

los.do: Build a solvated, ionized protein box in CHARMM-GUI Solution Builder at the experimental temperature, pH and salt, deciding which crystallographic components and termini to keep.
ek: Keep crystallographic waters for the folded protein (pockets refill slowly); drop BME/Cl⁻ additives unless relevant; set temperature to the experiment (often 298.15 K, not the 303.15 K default).

los.do: Order the preparation stages — minimize, assign velocities, restrained NVT, NPT, production — and justify each stage.
ek: Minimize to remove clashes; relax solvent at constant volume with solute restrained; then relax volume at constant pressure; NVT production at a set density needs NPT equilibration first.

los.do: Calculate the per-component velocity spread or RMS speed of an atom drawn from a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution — numeric rep.
ek: σ_v = √(k_BT/m) per Cartesian component; v_rms = √(3k_BT/m).

los.do: Decide when equilibration is complete from time series of energy, temperature, pressure, density and RMSD, and discard the burn-in.
ek: No drift and fluctuation about a stable mean in several observables; if unsure, extend. Analyse only the production portion, applying the cut uniformly.

los.do: Compute a normalized autocorrelation function and integrated correlation time from a short time series — numeric rep.
ek: C_j = ⟨δx_k δx_{k+j}⟩ / s²; τ_int = Σ_j C_j, summed until it converges but before it integrates noise.

los.do: Calculate the statistical inefficiency and effective number of independent samples, and from them the standard error of a mean — numeric rep.
ek: g = 1 + 2Σ_{j≥1} C_j (in frames); N_ind = N/g; s(x̄) = s(x)/√N_ind. Saving frames more often than τ adds disk, not information.

los.do: Compute a standard error from block averages and identify the block size at which the estimate plateaus — numeric rep.
ek: Split N frames into M equal blocks of n; s(x̄) = s(block means)/√M; increase n until s(x̄) stops growing.

los.do: Compute a standard error and 95% confidence interval from n independent trials using the Student t factor — numeric rep.
ek: SE = s/√n with s over trial means; CI = x̄ ± t·SE, t(0.975, n − 1) = 2.78 for n = 5, 2.57 for n = 6. Starting structures must be independent for this to hold.

los.do: Propagate uncertainty through sums, differences and nonlinear functions, e.g. σ(ΔΔG) from two legs — numeric rep.
ek: Independent legs: σ²(a − b) = σ²_a + σ²_b; nonlinear F: σ²_F ≈ Σ(∂F/∂x_i)² σ²_i, valid when noise-to-signal is small.

los.do: Bootstrap a confidence interval for a derived quantity from correlated data, and report it with significant figures that match the uncertainty.
ek: Resample blocks or independent trials, not raw frames; 95% CI = 2.5th–97.5th percentile. Report the confidence level and only meaningful digits.

los.do: Distinguish statistical uncertainty from sampling error that no error bar reveals, and detect insufficient sampling from drift, rare transitions and disagreement between independent runs.
ek: Checks can rule out good sampling but never prove it. Independent runs from diverse starts that disagree beyond their error bars signal unvisited states ('dark uncertainty').

los.do: Calculate ΔA from given ⟨exp(−βΔU)⟩ or a list of ΔU samples with the Zwanzig relation, forward and reverse — numeric rep.
ek: ΔA_0→1 = −k_BT ln⟨exp(−βΔU)⟩_0, ΔU = U₁ − U₀ evaluated on state-0 samples; exact in the limit, derived from Q₁/Q₀.

los.do: Estimate ΔA from the mean and variance of ΔU with the second-order cumulant expansion — numeric rep.
ek: ΔA ≈ ⟨ΔU⟩₀ − βσ²_ΔU/2; exact for Gaussian ΔU.

los.do: Judge whether an FEP estimate is reliable from the ΔU distribution width and forward–reverse hysteresis.
ek: The exponential average is biased and dominated by rare low-ΔU samples; reliable only when σ_ΔU ≲ 1–2 k_BT, i.e. neighbouring states overlap. Large forward–reverse disagreement means too few windows.

los.do: Calculate ΔA by integrating ⟨∂U/∂λ⟩ over λ windows with the trapezoid or Simpson rule — numeric rep.
ek: ΔA = ∫₀¹ ⟨∂U/∂λ⟩_λ dλ; trapezoid needs evenly or explicitly weighted windows; Simpson needs an odd number of evenly spaced points.

los.do: Derive ∂U/∂λ for a linear mixing potential and explain why curvature near the endpoints demands more windows or soft-core.
ek: U = (1 − λ)U₀ + λU₁ ⇒ ∂U/∂λ = U₁ − U₀; for appearing atoms ⟨∂U/∂λ⟩ diverges as λ → 0 under linear LJ scaling.

los.do: Explain how BAR combines forward and reverse ΔU samples and why it beats one-sided exponential averaging.
ek: BAR solves a self-consistent equation for ΔA using both directions; it is the minimum-variance two-state estimator and much less biased than Zwanzig.

los.do: Explain MBAR as reweighting all samples to all states, and relate it to BAR and WHAM.
ek: MBAR solves for every state's free energy simultaneously from all samples; with two states it reduces to BAR; binned, it is WHAM (used in ALF flattening).

los.do: Read an MBAR overlap matrix and decide where to add λ states — choice rep.
ek: Each state should share substantial overlap with its neighbours (off-diagonal elements not near zero); a weak link between two neighbours is where to insert a state. 20–40 states are typical.

los.do: Design an alchemical λ schedule for inserting or deleting atoms: order of electrostatic and LJ changes, soft-core, and number of states.
ek: Remove charges while LJ cores are on, then transform LJ with soft-core, then restore charges on inserted atoms; never change both at once on linear paths when sites appear or vanish.

los.do: Explain the endpoint catastrophe and how soft-core potentials remove it.
ek: As an atom's LJ is scaled to zero, other atoms can overlap it and r⁻¹² diverges; soft-core remaps short distances so the energy stays finite (in MSλD, distances inside a λ-dependent cutoff, r₀ = 2 Å).

los.do: Distinguish single, dual and multiple topology and decoupling vs annihilation, and identify the topology MSλD uses — choice rep.
ek: MSλD uses a shared core plus one complete substituent group per alternative; substituents at the same site never interact with each other; decoupling turns off only intermolecular terms.

los.do: Close a thermodynamic cycle to compute a relative binding ΔΔG from alchemical legs in complex and solvent — numeric rep.
ek: ΔΔG_bind = ΔG_bind(B) − ΔG_bind(A) = ΔG_complex(A→B) − ΔG_solvent(A→B); the physical binding legs are never simulated.

los.do: Compute a mutational folding ΔΔG from alchemical legs in the folded protein and an unfolded-state peptide model, and state its sign convention — numeric rep.
ek: ΔΔG_fold = ΔG_alch(folded) − ΔG_alch(unfolded); positive = destabilizing. The capped pentapeptide (mutating residue ± 2) models a locally solvated unfolded state and ignores nonlocal contacts.

los.do: Compute cycle-closure errors in a perturbation network and use them to flag unreliable edges — numeric rep.
ek: ΔG summed around any closed loop should be 0; nonzero closure measures error. Star maps are cheap; redundant, connected maps allow error analysis.

los.do: Lay out the double-decoupling cycle with restraints and identify every term in ΔG°_bind, including the standard-state correction.
ek: Decouple the ligand in solvent and in the restrained site; add the restraint free energy (analytic for Boresch's six-DOF restraints) and the standard-state term; remove charges before LJ.

los.do: Calculate the standard-state correction for confining a ligand to a given restraint volume — numeric rep.
ek: ΔG = −k_BT ln(V_site/V°), V° = 1661 Å³ per molecule at 1 M.

los.do: Choose a relative or absolute calculation for a described project — choice rep.
ek: Relative: congeneric series with a shared core and a reliable bound pose. Absolute: no common substructure, uncertain site, or comparing sites or poses.

los.do: Convert between K_d and ΔG° and between fold-changes and ΔΔG, and judge a prediction against expected accuracy — numeric rep.
ek: ΔG° = RT ln(K_d/1 M); a 10× change in K_d is 1.36 kcal/mol at 298 K; ~1–2 kcal/mol RMS error is typical in favourable cases.

los.do: Match simulation conditions (pH, salt, temperature, construct, protonation) to the experiment being reproduced.
ek: The T4 lysozyme sites were measured at pH 3.0 (L99, M106, F153) and 5.4 (V149), so two folded-state setups are needed.

units.title: λ dynamics and multisite λ dynamics

los.do: Write the λ-dynamics extended Hamiltonian and explain how treating λ as a particle samples several alchemical states in one simulation.
ek: H = K(x) + ½ m_λ λ̇² + U(x, λ); λ moves under −∂U/∂λ with a fictitious mass, so its population over time reflects relative free energies.

los.do: Write the MSλD potential for several sites and substituents and identify which terms scale with λ.
ek: U = U₀ + Σ_s Σ_i λ_si U_si + Σ λ_si λ_tj U_si,tj (s ≠ t); Σ_i λ_si = 1 and λ_si ≥ 0 at each site; the environment U₀ is unscaled; substituents at one site don't see each other.

los.do: Calculate the number of λ variables and chemical end states for a multisite system from its nsubs list — numeric rep.
ek: nsubs counts native + each mutant per site (V149 with 5 mutants ⇒ 6); nblocks = Σ nsubs; end states = Π nsubs (15 sites × 2 ⇒ 32 768).

los.do: Compute λ values from θ coordinates with the fnex implicit constraint and verify they sum to one — numeric rep.
ek: λ_i = exp(c sin θ_i) / Σ_j exp(c sin θ_j), c = 5.5 (fnex); θ is unbounded, λ stays in (0, 1) and sums to 1 automatically.

los.do: Calculate the λ bounds an fnex constraint can reach for a given number of substituents and explain the endpoint error it causes — numeric rep.
ek: Bounds = [1 + (N − 1)e^{±2c}]⁻¹, so exact endpoints are never sampled (≈ 0.1–0.2 kcal/mol error) and sampling weakens past 8–9 substituents; piecewise constraints (fnpwise2026) reach the exact endpoints.

los.do: Identify the role of each ALF bias term — fixed φ (b), quadratic ψ (c), endpoint χ (x) and ω (s), and the newer t and u terms — on the alchemical landscape.
ek: φ offsets each substituent's free energy (≈ −ΔG) so all endpoints are equally populated; ψ_ij/4 changes the barrier between substituents; χ/ω shape the region near endpoints; bcxstu2026 adds t and u terms for many substituents.

los.do: Calculate the number of pairwise bias potentials a block setup must allocate for a given nblocks and bias scheme — numeric rep.
ek: Pairs = nblocks(nblocks − 1)/2; bcxs2018 uses 5 potentials per pair, bcxstu2026 uses 9 (ldbi count).

los.do: Calculate the free-energy difference between two substituents from their end-state populations (λ > 0.99) and fixed biases — numeric rep.
ek: ΔG_i→j = −k_BT ln(P_j/P_i) − (φ_j − φ_i), with P counted only where λ > λ_c (0.99 in production; 0.8 in older work).

los.do: Interpret nan or very noisy entries in Result.txt as unsampled substituents and decide whether to refine biases before extending production.
ek: A histogram estimator needs every end state visited; unvisited substituents mean biases are not yet converged — run another production of the same length first.

los.do: Describe one ALF cycle — run MD, reweight recent runs, compute 1-D and 2-D free-energy profiles, fit bias changes, write the next variables file — and why changes are capped.
ek: WHAM/MBAR combine several recent runs at different biases; a linear model of profile response feeds a quadratic penalty on deviations from flat. Only the bottom few kcal/mol of a basin is sampled, so updates are limited to a few kcal/mol.

los.do: Judge from PlotFreeEnergy5 profiles whether flattening has converged enough to start production.
ek: Sampling should extend across every profile with no large unsampled gaps; perfect flatness isn't required, thermodynamic accessibility is.

los.do: Plan the flattening schedule and convert it to step counts at a given timestep — numeric rep.
ek: initialize; ~100 runflat cycles of 100 ps (200 for arginine), equilibration = ¼ of each run (25 ps + 75 ps, so the sampling-steps argument is 3× the equilibration one); then ~10 cycles of 1 ns. At 2 fs, 25 ps = 12 500 steps.

los.do: Plan a production ramp of independent trials extended by factors of 4–5 to a target length, and total its simulation time — numeric rep.
ek: 5 trials (a–e) each round, e.g. 5 → 20 → 100 ns. Typical totals: solvation 10–20 ns; well-behaved protein point mutations 40 ns; hard or multiple mutations 100 ns; massive spaces 400 ns.

los.do: Write alf_info.py for a system: name, nsubs, nblocks, temp, enginepath, nreps, and optional q, loss, bias and impcons keys.
ek: name must match prep/name.inp; nblocks = Σ nsubs; nreps = 1 without replica exchange; q lists each substituent's net charge.

los.do: Choose loss function, bias scheme and implicit constraint for a described system — choice rep.
ek: Defaults linear2018 / bcxs2018 / fnex2011 are no longer best practice: use nonlinear2024 loss and fnpwise2026; bcxs2018 for ~2 substituents, bcxstu2026 for ~20 (with matching blocksetup.inp edits).

los.do: Compute ΔΔG_fold with its uncertainty from Result.txt values in the folded and unfolded ensembles — numeric rep.
ek: ΔΔG = dG(folded) − dG(unfolded) per mutant relative to native; combine the two legs' errors in quadrature.

topics.title: Building the alchemical system in CHARMM

los.do: Edit alchemical_definitions.inp for a mutation set: site resids, substituent sequence codes, segids and terminal variables.
ek: s1seq1 = 0 is the native residue; further entries are one-letter codes (h/b/j = HSD/HSE/HSP); nterres/cterres = first and last resid of the chain (1–162 folded, site ± 2 unfolded).

los.do: Assemble a prep directory — system.inp adapted from step5_production.inp, toppar soft link, aa_stream patch/select/delete/blocksetup streams, nbond.str, alf_info.py — and test it with RunSetup.
ek: DIMENS must be in the first script CHARMM reads, so it is removed from system.inp; patchloop adds alchemical atoms, selectloop names them, deleteloop removes spurious angles/dihedrals, blocksetup applies λ scaling and biases.

los.do: Compute the RMSD between two small coordinate sets after optimal superposition, and use RMSD vs time to judge stability before free-energy runs — numeric rep.
ek: RMSD = √[(1/N) Σ |r_i − r_i^ref|²] after Kabsch alignment on a chosen atom set (Cα or backbone); a plateau, not a small number, is the stability signal.

los.do: Compute per-residue RMSF and convert it to a crystallographic B-factor for comparison with experiment — numeric rep.
ek: RMSF_i = √⟨|r_i − ⟨r_i⟩|²⟩ after alignment; B = (8π²/3) RMSF².

los.do: Classify a contact as a hydrogen bond from donor–acceptor distance and angle under a stated criterion — choice rep.
ek: Common criterion: D···A ≤ 3.5 Å and D–H···A angle ≥ 120–150°; report occupancy as fraction of frames, and state the criterion used.

los.do: Cluster conformations by RMSD and report cluster populations and representative structures.
ek: Cutoff-based or hierarchical clustering on pairwise RMSD; combined clustering of independent runs tests whether they sample the same states.

los.do: Compute a potential of mean force from a histogram of a coordinate — numeric rep.
ek: W(ξ) = −k_BT ln P(ξ) + const; bins with no counts carry no information.

los.do: Load a trajectory correctly (PSF before DCD in VMD) and re-centre or unwrap periodic coordinates before measuring.
ek: A DCD holds only coordinates; the PSF supplies atom identities. Molecules split across box faces corrupt RMSD and distances until imaged.

los.do: Write a SLURM script for a GPU CHARMM job with partition, account, time limit, GPU request and memory, and submit or debug it without using the login node.
ek: -p free-gpu or gpu; -A rhayes1_lab_gpu on paid partitions only; --time in minutes; --gres=gpu:1 (a GPU partition alone gives no GPU); --mem only after an OOM; srun --pty for interactive debugging; --array=1-4%1 runs chained segments one at a time.

los.do: Estimate GPU-hours and cost for a simulation campaign from throughput in ns/day, and choose free vs paid partitions — numeric rep.
ek: GPU-h = 24 × total ns / (ns/day); paid gpu is $0.32 per GPU-hour; free-gpu costs nothing but jobs are preempted (ALF tolerates restarts).

los.do: Choose an engine — CHARMM standard, DOMDEC, BLaDE, OpenMM — for a described job — choice rep.
ek: Standard CHARMM is CPU and slow; DOMDEC GPU is ~5× slower than BLaDE; BLaDE runs MSλD 5–8× faster than DOMDEC; OpenMM is fast for plain MD but does not run λ dynamics within CHARMM.

los.do: Write BLaDE NVT and NPT dynamics commands and state BLaDE's restrictions.
ek: Add 'blade' to ENER/MINI/DYNA; NPT adds 'prmc iprs 100 pref 1 prdv 100'; set friction with 'scalar fbeta set 0.1 sele all end'. Langevin or NVE only, MC barostat only, H-bond constraints only, one GPU per OpenMP thread, no MPI.

los.do: Run an equivalent plain-MD simulation through OpenMM's Python API from CHARMM files.
ek: Load PSF + parameter set, build the System with PME and H-bond constraints, LangevinMiddleIntegrator at T, MonteCarloBarostat at 1 bar; CHARMM-GUI can emit OpenMM inputs directly.

los.do: Read and write CHARMM scripts using titles, set/calc, @ and @@ variables, ? system values, stream, if/goto loops, bomlev and stop, and find the right documentation section.
ek: Titles start with * and end at a lone *; ! starts comments; CHARMM is case-insensitive but file paths aren't (quote them). Key docs: BLOCK, CONSTRAINTS (SHAKE, restraints), Ewald, nonbonded, CRYSTAL and IMAGE.

los.do: Record everything needed to reproduce a run: force-field and engine versions, protonation states, box and ions, seeds, all scripts under version control, and unprocessed data.
ek: A result without its inputs and analysis scripts can't be checked; document the full uncertainty procedure too.

los.do: Estimate trajectory storage from atom count, save interval and simulation length — numeric rep.
ek: DCD stores single-precision x, y, z: 12 bytes per atom per frame; frames = steps / nsavc.

los.do: Clean up a finished ALF project, separating disposable intermediates from data that must be kept.
ek: run*/output, analysis*/data, Energy, Lambda and slurm logs are disposable; keep alchemical trajectories (run*/res) of published work; spatial DCDs may go after publication.

los.do: Decide whether intersite coupling biases are needed and set ntersite for flattening and postprocessing.
ek: Default [0,0] ignores coupling; with significant coupling use [0,1] in short runflat cycles and [2,1] in postprocess (adjusting only c intersite biases).

los.do: Choose between the histogram estimator and the Potts-model estimator (likelihood vs pseudolikelihood) for a given chemical-space size — choice rep.
ek: Histograms need every end state visited (~100–500 states max); Potts keeps one- and two-site terms only; LM below ~10⁶ end states, PLM above.

los.do: Partition a mutation set across sites and systems to respect substituent-per-site limits — choice rep.
ek: The ALF README advises ≤ 6 substituents per site (9 the tested ceiling); split larger sets across systems sharing a reference substituent. Newer constraints and biases (2024–2026) extend this to dozens.

los.do: Correct a charge-changing perturbation: explain its PME finite-size errors and apply ALF's discrete solvent correction with the q key.
ek: Net-charge changes in a neutral PME box introduce artifacts; the discrete solvent correction is the largest computable term; alternatives include co-alchemical ions.

los.do: Explain when a site needs replica exchange (e.g. A42, A98, M102 in T4 lysozyme) and how biasing-potential replica exchange helps.
ek: Some sites have slow coupled conformational and alchemical barriers; replicas with offset biases exchange to cross them. Replica runs need nreps > 1 and working MPI on the cluster.

los.do: Explain why proline and glycine mutations need a dedicated alchemical strategy.
ek: Proline bonds its side chain back to the backbone N and glycine lacks Cβ, so backbone terms (CMAP, ring closure) differ between substituents; Hayes & Brooks 2021 give the workaround.
